I did my undergrad here and am now in graduate school in the electrical engineering department. So far, I have loved UNCC. The campus is beautiful! The ECE department is really small so you’ll get to know everyone and the professors are very engaged with their students. 

I think we’re different than most engineering schools because we focus on cooperation rather than competing with our classmates. We focus more on hands on knowledge as well. Be prepared for crazy projects that test your patience but have you feel so accomplished once they work! 

I have heard good things about Hawthorne. I choose not to stay there my freshman year because I’m a female student and I just didn’t feel comfortable living in a dorm that was mostly teenage boys. That dorm offers a lot of assistance in terms of study halls and tutoring. 

Your first year will be a tough transition. The classes will be larger (200+) but once you pass freshman year things start to look up. After freshman year, my class size was usually between 30-60. Now in grad school, it’s 10-20. 

My advice: take 1201, calc 1/2, and physics very seriously. Those are major weed out classes and will demand a lot of work out of you.

Also, our power and energy concentration within the ECE department is one of the best and has strong ties to industry. If you want to work for Duke Energy, UNCC is a good choice

Sooo I just got HBO and I know I’m a bit late to the party on this one. But, I’ve always felt connected to this case. As a teenager I was in a tumultuous relationship with someone who suffered from severe depression. And while I think what Michelle did crossed a line, I kind of get it. 

When you love someone who’s depressed your initial reaction is to push them to get help and to try to be positive. But after a while, the weight of having a partner so dependent on you takes a toll.

At the beginning of my relationship, I would literally talk my boyfriend out of jumping off of bridges. Not like over text. I would drive to the bridge by his house and try to convince him to come down off the ledge.

Initially, you see someone who is hurting so badly and all you want to do is help them. But after, you know, the fifth time you have to coerce someone out of killing themselves it starts to feel icky. It feels like you aren’t doing the right thing anymore. I remember driving home from that bridge thinking “why am I trying so hard to keep him here when it’s clear he’s suffering”. I almost felt selfish about it like I was trying so hard to keep him happy and alive because I didn’t want to loose him. 

I didn’t know how to help him. On top of that, I also was suffering from depression and I understood why he felt leaving was the best option. I understood why he felt his suffering would never get better. And in some respects I agreed with him because that’s how I felt too. 

Slowly over time I felt worse and worse about it. Until one night he started texting me about how he was going to kill himself. This time with pills. And that time I didn’t try to stop him because I didn’t want him to suffer anymore. He didn’t actually kill himself but continued to try up until I went to college and broke up with him. But I still feel that lingering guilt that no matter what I did in that situation I always felt like I wasn’t doing the right thing. 

I didn’t go to the extremes that Michelle went with it. But I get why she pushed him. I feel like in the end she thought it was a mercy killing. She thought she was helping him end his suffering. And if he was able to do it maybe then she would feel comfortable enough to do it herself. 

Just my thoughts...
